newsitem.title: USA: Bomb hoax causes scare on Mexicana plane.
newsitem.headline: Bomb hoax causes scare on Mexicana plane.

text.p: A Mexicana Airlines passenger plane was evacuated on Wednesday at a California airport after the airline received a bomb threat, but the scare turned out to be a hoax, airport officials said.
"Mexicana directly received a bomb threat and immediately isolated the aircraft and the passengers," San Jose International Airport spokeswoman Cathy Gaskell said.
Mexicana flight 953, with 163 passengers and six crew members on board, was bound for Guadalajara, and was then scheduled to fly to Mexico City.
Authorities in San Jose, located about 40 miles (64 km) south of San Francisco, said the bomb threat was made to airline officials just before 9:30 a.m. local time (1730 GMT).

The threat was made to the airline's reservations desk and was immediately passed on to airport security. The caller told the airline "there was a bomb aboard the flight," Gaskell said. The plane was at the gate when the call came in.
Once passengers and crew were evacuated, San Jose police, the FBI and federal aviation officials searched the plane, its luggage and cargo for any explosives.
Gaskell said no explosives were found on board and investigators cleared the flight for departure at about 2:00 p.m. (2200 GMT) local time.
An airline spokesperson was not immediately available to comment on the incident.
In July, a Mexicana passenger plane bound for Mexico from Chicago had to turn back shortly after take-off due to a bomb threat.
Also in July, a written bomb threat found on board an Alaska Airlines plane caused a scare and delayed passengers for hours at the San Jose airport. That threat also turned out to be a hoax.
